title: Tic-tac-toe game design
idea: A tic-tac-toe design splits the game into cells, a turn order, a status, and a win check that updates counters instead of rescanning the board.
points: Each row, column and diagonal has a counter: X adds 1, O subtracts 1.
Mixed marks cancel out, so only a one-mark line reaches `n` or `-n`.
`play` validates first, then changes state, so a bad move leaves no trace.
A `Status` enum ends the game; later moves throw instead of passing silently.

code.title: Game with counters
code.caption: Seven scripted moves: one lands on a taken cell, one comes after the game is over.

walk.text: Two enums name every mark and every game status.
One counter per row, column and diagonal: `2n + 2` in all.
Reject the move before anything changes: game over or cell taken.
Add this move to its row, column and any diagonal it sits on.
Check only the lines this move touched. A full line wins; a full board draws.
Report the move, then flip the turn for the next player.
`main` plays the script and prints each result or rejection.

pitfalls: Check bounds before indexing `cells`; an off-board move throws `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`.
Do not rescan the whole board after each move; update the touched counters.
Flip the turn only after a valid move, or a rejection skips a player.

quiz.q: What is the fifth line `TicTacToeDemo` prints?
quiz.why: O already holds 1,1, so `play` throws before changing anything. The turn stays with X, who wins on the next move.

takeaway: Validate, update the counters, set the status, then flip the turn.
